thesis: Held position. Dell reported fiscal Q2 2027 on 2026-09-01 with record revenue of $47.0B, up 58% year over year, against a consensus near $44.9B. Both published profit metrics move the same way: GAAP diluted EPS of $6.34 (up 273%) and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $7.04 (up 203%), the latter against a consensus near $4.87-$4.92. Infrastructure Solutions revenue was reported at $31.78B, up 89%, with traditional servers and networking up 122% and storage up 26%; AI server backlog was disclosed at $95B and full-year FY27 guidance was raised to $24.37 GAAP / $25.50 non-GAAP EPS. The strongest counter-evidence is the specific bear case analysts carried into the print: surging server memory prices diluting a structurally thin infrastructure margin. That case does not survive the disclosure - non-GAAP operating margin came in at 12.6% of revenue with operating expenses up 22% against revenue up 58%, so this quarter showed margin expansion rather than the feared compression. The stock closed 2026-09-02 up on 7.85x its 30-bar average volume, consistent with the disclosed print rather than with an unexplained move. No active litigation with a scheduled ruling, hearing or compliance deadline in the next ~90 days surfaced in this run's research; the matters found (an ERISA 401(k) suit reported February 2026 and WSOU patent appeals docketed July 2026) carry no scheduled near-term date in what was read.
invalidation: A subsequent Dell disclosure showing AI-server gross margin compressing rather than expanding, a cut to the raised FY27 EPS guidance, or evidence that the $95B AI backlog is not converting to revenue at the guided pace.
sources: Dell Technologies investor relations, Q2 FY2027 results press release (2026-09-01): https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-second-quarter-fiscal-2027-financial

thesis: Held position. Nvidia reported fiscal Q2 2027 on 2026-08-26 for the quarter ended 2026-07-26: revenue of $96.2B, up 106% year over year and 18% sequentially, with Data Center at $89.02B, up 117%, on the Blackwell Ultra ramp. Adjusted EPS of $2.22 beat a $2.09 consensus. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were both reported at 75.0%, so the two profitability presentations agree rather than diverging. The company returned a record $26B to shareholders in the quarter ($20B buybacks, $6B dividends). The strongest counter-evidence is Nvidia's own guidance that gross margin will decline and bottom in fiscal Q4 2027 at 71-72%, partly on memory prices - a company-disclosed negative, not a rumor. It does not change the read because it is bounded and quantified by the company at a 71-72% trough while revenue is compounding at 106% year over year, so gross profit dollars still expand across the guided trough; a margin step-down of roughly three to four points on a base growing at that rate is a smaller effect than the revenue line. Separately, China's market regulator found in September 2025 that Nvidia violated the anti-monopoly law in connection with the 2020 Mellanox acquisition and said it would investigate further; this run's research found no scheduled ruling, hearing or compliance deadline for that matter, so it is noted here but not flagged.
invalidation: Gross margin guided or reported below the 71-72% trough the company disclosed, a sequential decline in Data Center revenue, or a Chinese regulatory action that attaches a specific penalty or scheduled deadline to the Mellanox finding.

thesis: Lumentum reported fiscal Q4 2026 on 2026-08-12: revenue of $1,006.3M, up 109.3% year over year and the company's first billion-dollar quarter, with adjusted EPS and revenue both roughly doubling year over year and both beating consensus, and gross margin crossing 50% ahead of the company's own schedule. Management guided fiscal Q1 materially above consensus on both revenue and earnings. The shares rose 13.63% on the print to $932.47, and Mizuho, JPMorgan, Raymond James, Citi and BNP Paribas raised targets. The strongest counter-evidence is that this is a name that has already run enormously - a 52-week range of $130.97 to $1,085.68 - so the objection is that the beat was already in the price, and the stock has since drifted back to $870.29 alongside the broader AI-optical derating that also hit Coherent. That objection does not change the read here because the company raised its own forward number at the same time: the fiscal Q1 guide was set materially above consensus, so the disclosed forward earnings base moved up with the price rather than lagging it, which is the specific thing a 'priced-in' argument requires to be false. This run's research surfaced no equity raise, no C-suite departure, and no litigation with a scheduled near-term date.
invalidation: Fiscal Q1 revenue or EPS landing below the guidance range management set, gross margin falling back under 50%, or a disclosed order cut or push-out from a major AI data-center customer.

thesis: AST SpaceMobile is 22.6% lower over the trimmed 60-day window but rose 9.43% on 2026-09-02. In its 2026-08-10 business update and Q2 2026 results the company disclosed that revenue more than doubled sequentially on government and commercial contracts, with a backlog of $1.3B and more than $3.7B in cash, and guided 2026 revenue to $150M-$200M. BlueBird satellites 11-13 were launched, moving the constellation toward beta space-based cellular broadband. Cantor Fitzgerald raised its target to $90 with an Overweight rating, citing a possible 2027 revenue floor near $500M while explicitly flagging heavy free-cash-flow burn, and director Adriana Cisneros bought 10,822 shares for about $619,200 on 2026-08-31. The counter-case is that burn: a pre-scale operator building a satellite constellation consumes cash faster than $150M-$200M of revenue replaces it, and the disclosed $3.7B cash balance funds that for now rather than removing the question. What holds conviction to medium rather than higher is that the near-term value here still turns on an unresolved binary: the launch and beta-service cadence. A launch or deployment failure in the next few months would reverse the read, and this thesis cannot settle that in advance.
invalidation: A launch or satellite-deployment failure, 2026 revenue tracking below the $150M-$200M guidance, a new equity or convertible raise materially below the current price, or the disclosed backlog failing to convert into recognised revenue.
sources: Business Wire, AST SpaceMobile Q2 2026 business update: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260810780163/en/AST-SpaceMobile-Provides-Business-Update-and-Second-Quarter-2026-Results

thesis: Corcept is 20.5% higher over the trimmed 60-day window, and the move is traceable to a specific disclosed event rather than to drift: on 2026-07-30 the company reported Q2 2026 EPS of $0.36 against a $0.05 consensus and revenue of $256.1M against $220.1M, and raised 2026 revenue guidance to $1.1B-$1.2B. The stock gapped from about $112 to a $122.21 high and closed at $119.08 on roughly 2.94M shares against a ~539k 30-bar average, so the largest bar in the window is explained by the print. Management also disclosed launch metrics for LIFYORLI (relacorilant), approved by the FDA in March 2026 in combination with nab-paclitaxel for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer and selling since April: more than 1,300 patients started on treatment and more than 1,000 physicians having prescribed it at least once. The counter-case is the regulatory history on the same molecule - the FDA issued a Complete Response Letter on 2025-12-31 for relacorilant in hypertension secondary to hypercortisolism, and Corcept resubmitted that NDA on 2026-06-17 - together with securities suits that this run's sources reference around the CRL. That counter-case bears on a different indication than the one driving the beat and the guidance raise, which is the argument for holding the read. Conviction stops at medium because the resubmitted NDA carries an FDA action date this run could not confirm, leaving an unresolved binary regulatory catalyst of unknown timing; no litigation with a specific scheduled date within ~90 days was found, so none is flagged.
invalidation: A second Complete Response Letter on the resubmitted hypercortisolism NDA, 2026 revenue tracking below the raised $1.1B-$1.2B guidance, a slowdown in disclosed LIFYORLI prescriber or patient-start counts, or a scheduled court date emerging in the securities litigation.

thesis: Held position. The evidence this run is genuinely offsetting rather than net-positive, and that is why this is rated low. On the supportive side, the quarter ended 2026-07-29 was reported at $90.01B revenue and $4.74 EPS, Azure crossed $100B in annual revenue, and commercial backlog was disclosed up 84% to $678B - contracted future revenue, not a projection. Against that, Microsoft spent about $115.9B-$116B on AI capex in fiscal 2026, roughly 4.5x the $6.8B it paid in dividends, and free cash flow fell 6%; the forward capex figure was revised from about $190B guided in April to about $175B, though sources attribute part of that change to a revision in the expected useful life of data centres and office buildings rather than to a genuine spending cut, which is exactly the ambiguity this thesis cannot resolve. The stock is 28.5% higher over the trimmed 60-day window while sitting 9.6% below its 52-week high, and it touched a one-year low earlier in the cycle on these same spending concerns. Backlog growth of 84% and free cash flow down 6% point in opposite directions, and this run's research does not settle which dominates, so the counter-case is named and unanswered. No litigation with a scheduled ruling, hearing or deadline in the next ~90 days surfaced: the FTC's Activision matter was dropped in May 2025 and the broader FTC inquiry appears to remain at the investigation stage with no scheduled proceeding found.
invalidation: Azure growth decelerating further while capex guidance rises again, free cash flow falling for a second consecutive period, a write-down or impairment on AI infrastructure, or a scheduled regulatory proceeding attaching to the open FTC inquiry.

thesis: Astera Labs is 36.65% lower over the trimmed 60-day window, which is a large adverse move against disclosed results that were strong, so this run searched twice to reconcile it. The disclosures: Q2 2026, reported 2026-08-04, showed record revenue of $392.4M, up 27% sequentially and 104% year over year and about 8.8% above consensus, with non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.80 against a $0.69 estimate, and Q3 guidance of $540M-$560M on the Scorpio X-Series 320-lane fabric switch ramp - a beat and a raise. The reconciliation the sources offer is that the decline is positioning rather than fundamentals: the stock rose four sessions into the print, including 20.0% on 2026-07-30 and 12.7% the day before the report, then gave back that gain, and the wider move sits inside a sector-wide derating of highly valued AI-infrastructure names, with higher operating expenses from continued product-roadmap investment cited as the only company-specific negative. That explanation is sentiment- and positioning-driven and discounts the fundamental significance of the drop, which is precisely why this is rated low rather than higher: the disclosed numbers and the tape disagree by a wide margin, and the resolution offered is a technical one this run cannot verify independently. Analyst targets moving in the opposite direction to the price (TD Cowen to $425 from $225, Bank of America to $450 from $240, both keeping non-buy ratings) is itself unresolved evidence rather than support. Note this symbol appears in get_account_positions with a position of 0, i.e. not held.
invalidation: Q3 revenue landing below the $540M-$560M guided range, operating expenses continuing to outrun revenue growth, loss of the Scorpio ramp at a major customer, or a further decline on a disclosed company-specific negative rather than on sector moves.

thesis: AMD is 17.2% lower over the trimmed 60-day window on evidence that is genuinely mixed. The company's Q2 2026 results were a beat on both lines - EPS of $1.66 ahead of estimates and revenue of $11.55B above consensus - yet the shares fell after the report, which sources attribute to expectations having been set very high for AI names rather than to anything disclosed. The wider decline is sector-driven: the largest semiconductor stocks lost roughly $1 trillion of combined market capitalisation in July, and chip names including AMD sold off again in late August after the Fed chair's Jackson Hole remarks. Two company-relevant negatives sit alongside that and are not settled here: a report that DeepSeek is developing its own AI processor, and a report that SpaceX selected Nvidia rather than AMD. Valuation is the third strand, with a trailing P/E cited near 123 against a tech-sector average near 35. This is rated low because the read does not resolve into a clear net direction - a confirmed beat, a sentiment- and sector-driven drawdown, and unquantified competitive losses offset one another, and this run's research does not establish which dominates.
invalidation: A guidance cut or data-centre revenue miss in the next report, confirmation that named AI customers are designing AMD out, or further multiple compression accompanied by a disclosed fundamental deterioration rather than sector moves.

thesis: Marvell is 17.2% lower over the trimmed 60-day window against a fiscal Q2 2027 report on 2026-08-27 that was strong on every disclosed line: record revenue of $2.006B, up 58% year over year and 6% sequentially; non-GAAP EPS of $0.67, up 123% year over year; data-centre revenue up 69% year over year on AI demand; and non-GAAP operating margin expanded 870 basis points year over year to 34.8%. The shares fell after the print anyway. The reason the sources give is specific rather than atmospheric - investors wanted more visibility into the recently announced $12.2B custom-chip agreement with Google, particularly its structure and timing - and that is the counter-case this thesis cannot answer: nothing this run read discloses the revenue phasing, margin profile or exclusivity terms of that agreement, so the market's stated objection stands unresolved. A stock up 195.8% year to date and 253.2% over one year going into the report is also carrying expectations that a beat alone may not clear. Naming a counter-case that cannot be settled from this run's sources is the low trigger, and that is the rating here rather than an escape from it.
invalidation: Disclosure that the $12.2B Google agreement carries materially lower margins or slower phasing than assumed, data-centre growth decelerating below the reported 69%, or the next guide falling short of consensus.

thesis: Applied Optoelectronics is 16.4% lower over the trimmed 60-day window, and the operating disclosures and the financing disclosure point in opposite directions. On 2026-08-06 the company reported Q2 2026 revenue of $191.9M, up 86% year over year and a fifth consecutive record quarter, with a swing back to non-GAAP profitability at adjusted EPS of $0.06 against $0.02 expected, and guided Q3 revenue up to $290M on 800G and 1.6T products; Rosenblatt initiated a Buy on 2026-08-07, and a reported draft FCC ban on new Chinese optical transceivers would, if adopted, favour non-Chinese suppliers. Against that, the company announced a further $600M at-the-market equity offering and the shares fell about 12.3% pre-market on the news. That ATM programme is a disclosed equity issuance within the last ~90 days and is flagged as dilution_risk below; a $600M ATM is large relative to this company and represents a standing supply overhang rather than a one-time event, which is the specific reason the operating momentum does not settle the read. The presence of a risk flag caps conviction at low under the rubric, and the evidence here justifies that independently.
invalidation: Q3 revenue falling short of the $290M guide, further ATM issuance beyond the announced $600M, non-GAAP profitability reversing, or the draft FCC transceiver restriction being dropped.

thesis: Sandisk is 10.95% lower over the trimmed 60-day window, a pullback inside a very large advance - sources put the stock up about 525% in 2026. The company-disclosed event in the window is an investor day held 2026-08-13, at which management set long-term targets of double-digit revenue growth through 2030 and an 80% non-GAAP gross margin, framed around tight NAND supply, AI-driven demand and long-term customer contracts. Sources describe recent supply agreements carrying a floor price of roughly $0.29 per gigabyte, and Bernstein raised its target to $3,000 from $1,700 on an Outperform rating, arguing those agreements offer more downside protection than the prior take-or-pay structures. The counter-case is that the same disclosure limits the upside case: the cited floor price is described as broadly in line with Q2 2026 average selling prices, so the contracts protect against a NAND price decline rather than implying one is coming from a higher base, and after a 525% run the derating risk in a cyclical memory name is real. This run cannot settle whether contracted floors near current ASPs are a strength or a ceiling - a named and unanswered counter-case - and the catalyst itself is forward-looking multi-year guidance rather than a completed result, so this is low.
invalidation: NAND spot or contract pricing falling below the cited floor levels, a disclosed reduction in long-term supply agreements, gross margin tracking well short of the 80% non-GAAP target, or a demand air-pocket in AI storage.
sources: Forbes Investor Hub, SanDisk stock up 574%: https://www.forbes.com/sites/investor-hub/article/sandisk-stock-over-574-where-its-heading-2026/

thesis: Intel is 26.3% lower over the trimmed 60-day window, and the decline is explained by disclosed, company-specific events rather than by sector drift alone. The company priced an upsized secondary offering of 210.5 million new shares at $95, lifting total proceeds to about $20B from an earlier $15B target, and the shares fell roughly 2-4% around the initial headlines on dilution; sources describe a continuing supply overhang from that offering through late August. Alongside it, Intel Foundry Services posted an operating loss of $2.8B in Q2 2026, with projections cited for more than $10B of cumulative operating losses through the end of 2027 before profitability. Product-side pressure is also disclosed: client computing group revenue down 8% year over year and data centre and AI revenue down 2%, against AMD's competitive position, with sources reporting Intel CPU market share at a three-decade low. The strongest counter-evidence for a bearish read is that the $20B raise removes financing risk from the foundry build-out and that strategic and government interest in domestic capacity is real. That does not change the call in the near term: the raise funds a business the company itself guides to consume more than $10B further before it earns anything, so the balance-sheet benefit is paid for with immediate dilution against losses that continue for years. Conviction is medium rather than higher because dilution overhang, foundry losses and a sector-wide semiconductor selloff all contribute and this run cannot establish which dominates the 60-day move.
invalidation: Foundry operating losses narrowing faster than the guided path, a major external foundry customer win, client or data-centre revenue returning to year-over-year growth, or the offering overhang clearing without further issuance.

thesis: Corning is 26.0% lower over the trimmed 60-day window. Two contributors are identifiable and neither supports an entry here. First, a company-disclosed one: Q2 results released 2026-07-28 were followed by a sharp sell-off, with third-quarter guidance described as coming in slightly below consensus. Second, a customer-demand item that is reported rather than company-disclosed: shares fell 2.7% after reports that Apple scrapped its planned all-glass 20th-anniversary iPhone, with a Jefferies downgrade of Apple citing supply-chain checks and poor production yields, for a handset that had been scheduled for a September 2027 launch. The stock fell 16% over five consecutive sessions, erasing roughly $24B of market value from a base near $125B, and fell 4.7% on 2026-08-19 alone. The strongest counter-evidence is that the Apple item concerns a single unreleased model two years out and is a third-party report, not a Corning disclosure or a stated order cut - so it is possible the demand impact is smaller than the price reaction implies. That does not change the call, because it does not stand alone: the guidance shortfall is the company's own number, and a soft forward guide plus a credible demand question at a key customer is not a setup that needs to be entered before either resolves. Conviction is medium because the two contributors are not separable from this run's evidence and neither is clearly dominant.
invalidation: Corning guiding above consensus in the next quarter, a company disclosure quantifying the Apple programme as immaterial, or confirmation that specialty-glass demand is unaffected by the cancelled model.

thesis: Rocket Lab is 32.2% lower over the trimmed 60-day window while its disclosed operating news was strongly positive, so this run searched a second time to reconcile the gap. The positives are confirmed: roughly $663M of combined U.S. Space Force awards over an eight-day span, comprising a $397M satellite development award and a record $266M launch-services deal; onboarding into the Space Data Network Consortium with two delivery orders totalling $12M; the 93rd Electron mission flown 2026-08-21 deploying an iQPS QPS-SAR satellite; and expiry of the U.S. Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period on the Iridium transaction at 11:59 p.m. ET on 2026-08-12. The reconciliation is a deal overhang the first search did not surface: SpaceX has challenged Iridium's conduct before the FCC as it reviews Rocket Lab's pending $8B takeover, and the shares fell 6% to $63.82 on that. The mechanism matters - the deal consideration ties Iridium payouts to Rocket Lab's own share price near closing through a variable exchange ratio, so regulatory delay transmits directly into the stock, and sources describe at-the-market share issuance and Neutron timing as live dilution questions alongside the equity component of the acquisition. A shareholder vote is scheduled for 2026-09-24. This is avoid rather than long because an unresolved binary regulatory and shareholder-vote event sits three weeks ahead with a self-referencing price mechanism attached, and the contract wins do not offset that in the interim. Conviction is low: the counter-case is engaged and cannot be settled before those events. No litigation flag is recorded because no specific scheduled FCC ruling date was found in what this run read, though the proceeding itself is real.
invalidation: FCC clearance of the Iridium transaction and a favourable 2026-09-24 shareholder vote, resolution of the SpaceX complaint, or a Neutron milestone that removes the financing and dilution question.

thesis: SpaceX is 12.3% lower over the trimmed 60-day window and the evidence is unresolved in both directions. Its first earnings report as a public company, on 2026-08-04, beat revenue estimates yet the stock fell about 8% in extended trading, with sources attributing the reaction to disclosed capital expenditure rather than to the revenue line. The wider move is much larger than the window shows: sources describe the shares falling from about $192 to roughly $108 and the implied valuation round-tripping from about $2.5 trillion to about $1.4 trillion after that first report, with the stock later recovering to $140.36. Two further pressures are identified and neither is settled: an August IPO lockup expiration making a significant block of shares eligible for sale, and a technical item from the 13th Starship test flight in July, where the company had trouble reigniting Raptor engines on the first stage - a failure mode that, if repeated during a landing at the launch site, would cause severe pad damage. The counter-case for a constructive read is that heavy capex in a launch and constellation business is investment rather than overspend, and revenue did beat. This thesis cannot settle that question from what it read, and a beat that the market met with an 8% decline on spending is precisely the kind of unresolved evidence the rubric rates low. Avoid rather than long: the capex trajectory, the lockup supply and the Starship relight issue are all open at once.
invalidation: A second quarter showing capex moderating or converting to disclosed revenue, successful Starship flights including a clean first-stage relight and landing, or the lockup supply clearing without sustained pressure.

thesis: LYTE qualified on the near-52-week-low criterion at 0.77% above its low, but that signal is close to meaningless for this instrument and the screening output makes it visible: the Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF began trading on 2026-08-06, and get_price_history returned only 20 bars, so its '52-week' low is really its since-inception low four weeks after launch. There is no company-disclosed catalyst to evaluate. The fund is actively managed and invests in equities of companies whose core technology involves generating, manipulating, detecting or transmitting light - optical transceivers, lasers, silicon photonics, optical interconnects, photodetectors, fibre infrastructure and optical computing - with an eligibility screen of roughly 50% of revenue from those areas, a 0.65% expense ratio, quarterly rebalancing, and total return swaps used for RIC diversification compliance. It is not leveraged or inverse, so it is not excluded by the universe filter, but it is a thematic sector vehicle: any thesis here would be a call on AI-optics sentiment as a whole rather than on a company-specific catalyst, which is a low trigger under the rubric. Its drift toward the inception low is also consistent with the same AI-optical derating this run documented in Coherent and Lumentum, rather than with anything the fund itself disclosed. Avoid pending an actual trading history and a company-specific reason to own it.
invalidation: Not applicable as a directional call - this would become evaluable once the fund has a genuine 52-week trading history, or if the underlying AI-optics thesis were expressed through a single-name holding with a disclosed catalyst instead.
